paragraphs: Meachar deqayma lan en binyan usetira bekelim, lepikak, delet shel shidda sheqqorin bearbe "dulab" (aron), shehu metaltel veeno banuy bekotel o baqqarqa; veken delet shel teba umigdal shehem metaltelin, vehaddelatot shellahem enam mechubbarim bahem bemasmerim ella nishlapim mehem, muttar leyittelem mehem, mishshum deen binyan usetira bekelim; abal lehachaziram aseru chaza"l, gezera shemma yitqa bachazaqa besakkin vitedot. veim hakkelim haelleh mechubbarim bakkotel o baqqarqa, asur - ben littol, ben lehachazir - dikyavan dimchubbarim baqqarqa, ikka binyan usetira bahasarat haddelatot ubachazaratam. vaapillu al-yede goy asur littol o lehachazir, vaapillu betzirim haasuyim bebarzel shehachor rachab, sheyyekolin littol ulehachazir beli shum ummanut, gam ken asur. vetzarik lehazhir hamon haam bazeh, ki poh irenu nikshalim bedabar zeh kamma bene-adam bidlatot shel chadarim, kesheyyobad hammapteach shellahem, darkam lishlop haddelet min hatztzad kede lehikkanes lacheder; veken bechallonot sheosim beqarqa hechatzer lemala mikkippat hammartep, veosim lahem delatot, delipamim nikshalim vesholepim haddelet legamre meal hachallon.

clarification.explanation: The basic rule: the law of "building and demolishing" does not apply to vessels (movable objects), only to things attached to the ground or a wall. Therefore the door of a cabinet ("dolab"), which is a movable vessel not attached to a wall or the ground, and likewise doors of a chest or cupboard that are not fastened with nails but simply slide out — may be removed on the Sabbath, since there is no actual "demolishing" here. But the Sages forbade putting them back — a decree lest one come to wedge them in forcefully with a knife or peg, thereby entering into a full prohibition of repairing. By contrast, if these doors are attached to the ground or a wall, it is forbidden both to remove and to replace them, since here there truly is a law of building and demolishing. This prohibition is severe to the extent that even asking a gentile to do so is forbidden; and even if the hinges are made of iron with a wide hole such that they can be removed and replaced very easily without any skill — it is still forbidden. Rabbi Yosef Chaim warns that in Baghdad people often fail in this: when the key to a room is lost, it was customary to slide the door out from the side to enter; and likewise at basement entrances in the courtyard floor, sometimes the door is slid entirely out of the window frame — and this is forbidden.
takeaways: A door of a movable vessel (cabinet, chest) may be removed on the Sabbath but not replaced, lest one wedge it in forcefully.
A door attached to a wall or the ground may neither be removed nor replaced, even through a gentile.
One must be especially careful when a key to a room or basement is lost — the door may not be slid out.

paragraphs: Kelim gedolim harbeh shemmachaziqin arbaim sea, dehaynu hem amma al amma berum shalosh ammot, "p sheen mechubbarim baqqarqa, asur littol diltutam.

clarification.explanation: Even very large vessels — those holding forty se'ah (that is, the size of a cubit by a cubit and three cubits in height) — even though not actually attached to the ground, have the severe law of attached things, and therefore it is forbidden to remove their doors on the Sabbath. The reason: because of their size and permanence they are considered like a fixed structure rather than an ordinary movable vessel.
takeaways: A vessel of enormous size (40 se'ah, roughly a cubit by a cubit and 3 cubits high) is considered attached to the ground for this purpose.
It is forbidden to remove its doors on the Sabbath even though it is not actually attached.

paragraphs: Delatot sheyyesh bahem shene tzirim - im yatza tzir hattachton kullo mimmeqomo, asur lehachaziro; veim miqtzato, muttar lehachaziro, veen chosheshin shemma yitqa, lepi sheen tzarik kol kak lazeh; abal im yatza tzir haelyon apillu miqtzato, asur lidchaqu ulehachaziro limqomo, gezera shemma yitqa, mippene shehaelyon tzarik lehaddeqo bechozeq yoter min hattachton, mippene shehattachton mitqayyem meelayv bechoro keshehaelyon bimqomo.

clarification.explanation: A door with two hinges (upper and lower): if the lower hinge has come entirely out of its place — it is forbidden to put it back. But if only part of it has come out — it is permitted to put it back, since there is no concern one will come to wedge it in forcefully, as the lower hinge settles into its hole on its own once the upper hinge is in place. By contrast, if the upper hinge has come out — even only partly — it is forbidden to push it back into place, out of concern one might come to wedge it in forcefully, since the upper hinge requires tighter wedging than the lower one in order to hold.
takeaways: A lower hinge that came out entirely — may not be replaced; if only part came out — permitted, since one will not come to wedge it.
An upper hinge — even if only partly out — may not be replaced, since it requires forceful wedging and there is concern one might jam it in.

paragraphs: Keli shel peraqim shennitpareq, kegon mitta shel peraqim vekayyotze, asur lehachaziro beshabbat apillu im eno mehaddeqo ella meat beinyan shehu rapuy veeno rapuy, gezera shemma yitqa bechozeq. vekol keli sheddarko lihyot maqpidin alayv sheyyihyeh mehuddaq vetaqua bechozeq, ap sheakshav rotzeh lehannicho rapuy - asur lehachaziro, gezera shemma yitqa. vehinneh poh irenu bagdad y" osim arisa shel peraqim baabur hattinoq. shemmebiim shene ammudim sheyyesh lekol echad shene raglayim, umaamidim otam echad miyyamin veechad missemol, umaknisim betokam ammud echad, shatucha benehem meeber leeber, vetolim haarisa bazeh haammud hattikon, vedarkam shel ellu lehaqpid sheyyihyeh rashe haammud hattikon mehuddaqim betok otam hashshenayim haomedim miyyamin umissemol; veal ken im nitparequ, asur lehachaziram beshabbat. vegam tzarik lehazhir poh irenu bemanul shel etz sheqqorin bearbi "g'lq" (mapteach etz), shehammapteach darko lihyot rosho menuqqab, umaknisim banneqabim shalosh o arba etzim qetannim sheal yadam niptach hammanul; veim napelu ellu haetzim min hanneqabim, asur lehachaziram, ki beellu maqpidim sheyyihyu mehuddaqim, deim lav, en yekolim liptoach hammanul; veken tzarik lehazhiram bekol kayyotze bazeh.

clarification.explanation: A vessel made of parts (such as a disassembling bed) that has come apart — it is forbidden to reassemble it on the Sabbath, even if one intends to leave it loose and not tightened at all, due to the decree lest one come to wedge it forcefully. And generally: any vessel that people are normally particular about having well tightened — it is forbidden to reassemble on the Sabbath even if one currently intends to leave it loose, since there is concern one might ultimately tighten it. Rabbi Yosef Chaim gives a local Baghdad example: an infant's cradle made of two side posts each with two legs, and a flat middle post between them from side to side, on which the cradle hangs — it is customary to make sure the middle post is well wedged into the two side posts, and therefore if it came apart — it is forbidden to reassemble it on the Sabbath. One should likewise be careful with a wooden lock ("jalaq") whose key is perforated and into which three or four small wooden pegs are inserted that operate the lock — if the pegs fell out of the holes, it is forbidden to put them back, since they must be well wedged in for the lock to function; and the same applies to anything similar.
takeaways: A disassembled vessel (such as a bed) may not be reassembled on the Sabbath even without tightening, out of concern one might come to wedge it forcefully.
The rule: a vessel normally kept tightly assembled may not be reassembled on the Sabbath even if one currently intends only a loose connection.
Example: a disassembled infant's cradle, and a wooden lock whose pegs fell out — both are forbidden to reassemble.

paragraphs: Kos shel peraqim shennitpareq, yesh oserin lehachaziro veyesh mattirin. vekosot shel peraqim hannimtzaim bazzeman hazzeh, lekulle alema asur lehachaziran, mishshum dedarkan lihyot mehuddaqim. ukeli sheqqorin bearbi "qumqum" (mezallep) vekayyotze bo, sheharosh shello asuy charitzim, kemo zeh sheqqorin bearbe "berege" (habraga), vehu mitpareq umitchabber al-yede hacharitzim, muttar lepareqo ulehachaziro beshabbat; v"p shemmehaddeqo bechozeq, en bo issur - lo bintila mishshum setira, velo bachazara mishshum binyan - lepi sheen asuyim leqiyyum kede sheyyihyeh bahem setira ubinyan, ella asuyin liptoach velisgor tamid, sheen hammashqeh niknas letok hakkeli o yotze mittoko ki im "y peticha o segira zot; vekol keha dedarko bekak, muttar, vekannizkar bapposeqim.

clarification.explanation: A disassembling cup (made of parts) that came apart — there is a dispute whether it may be reassembled on the Sabbath. But the disassembling cups found nowadays — all authorities forbid reassembling them, since they are normally kept tightly fastened, and this law is like that of other tightly-fastened vessels. By contrast, a vessel such as a kettle (spray container) that has an upper part with screw threads (like a threaded faucet) that comes apart and connects by screwing — it is permitted to disassemble and reassemble it on the Sabbath, and even if tightened forcefully there is no prohibition at all, neither demolishing in disassembly nor building in assembly. The reason: such vessels are not made to remain permanently fixed in a way that would carry the law of building and demolishing, but their entire purpose is to be opened and closed repeatedly — since the beverage enters and exits only through repeated opening and closing. Anything normally used this way is permitted.
takeaways: A disassembling cup nowadays — forbidden to reassemble on the Sabbath, since it is normally kept tightly fastened.
A vessel with screw threads (such as a kettle) meant to be opened and closed repeatedly — permitted to disassemble and reassemble even with forceful tightening.

paragraphs: Sapsal shennishmeta achat meraglayv, asur lehachazirah shabbat. vehattoqea etz beetz, hare zeh toledet boneh, vechayyab. veken hattoqea etz betok haqqardom o hassakkin vehammazleg bayyad shello, chayyab.

clarification.explanation: A bench that lost one of its legs — it is forbidden to put it back on the Sabbath. One who wedges a piece of wood into another piece of wood is considered to be performing a derivative of the labor of "building," and is Torah-liable for it. In the same way, one who wedges a wooden handle into an axe, knife, or fork is liable, since this too is considered an act of building.
takeaways: A bench leg that came off may not be put back on the Sabbath.
Wedging wood into wood (such as a handle into a tool) is considered a derivative of the labor of building and carries liability.

paragraphs: Kol hakkelim sheyyesh lahem delatot - ben shehaddelet min hatztzad, ben shehu kissuy al gabbe hakkelim - venitparequ haddelatot mehem; ben shennitparequ qodem shabbat, ben shennitparequ beshabbat, muttar letaltel et haddelatot, veen bahem issur muqtzeh, mippene shebbeet shehayu mechubbarim bekelim, haya gam alehem shem "keli" aggab abihen; v"p sheatta nitparequ, lo paqa mehem shem "keli". vekol zeh bidlatot shel hakkelim, abal daltot habbayit o shel chadarim vaaliyyot vekayyotze shennitparequ - ben beshabbat, ben qodem shabbat - muqtzim hem veasur letaltelam beshabbat; v"p sherauy lehishtammesh bahem atta betashmish shel nesarin - en muttarin betiltul, lepi shehen omedot lebayit achar shabbat, veen omedot lehishtammesh kishar nesarim.

clarification.explanation: Vessels with doors (whether a side door or a lid on top) whose doors have come apart from them — whether they came apart before the Sabbath or on the Sabbath itself — it is permitted to handle the doors themselves, and there is no prohibition of muktzeh regarding them. The reason: while the doors were attached to the vessel, the designation "vessel" applied to them as well (they are "dragged along" after the main vessel, their "parent"), and even though they have now come apart, the status of vessel that already applied to them has not lapsed. But this rule applies only to doors of vessels. By contrast, doors of the house itself, of rooms or attics, that came apart — whether before the Sabbath or on the Sabbath — are muktzeh, and it is forbidden to handle them on the Sabbath. This is so even though they are now fit for use as ordinary wooden planks (boards), since they are intended to return to serving as the house's doors after the Sabbath, and are not considered plain wooden planks.
takeaways: A door that came apart from a vessel (not from a house) may be handled, since the designation "vessel" already applied to it.
A door that came apart from a house, room, or attic is muktzeh and may not be handled, even though it is currently fit for use as a wooden plank.

paragraphs: Dabar sheen torat keli alayv sheasao kissuy likli, naasa alayv torat keli al-yede ken umuttar letaltelo kishar kelim; vehu shettiqqenu veasa bo maaseh vehekino lekak beinyan shettiqquno mokicha alayv shehu omed lekak, v"p sheadayin lo nishtammesh bo lekissuy meolam. veim nishtammesh bo lekissuy mibbeod yem apillu paam achat, zehu torat keli shello umuttar letaltelo beshabbat, "p shello asa bo shum maaseh shel tiqqun. bammeh debarim amurim? bedabar sheddarko laasoto lekissuy, kegon chatika shel nesarim vekayyotze bahen, abal dabar sheen darko laasoto kissuy, "p shennishtammesh bedabar zeh lekissuy peamim rabbot bechol, kegon eben shekkissa bah et pi hechabit peamim rabbot, asur letaltelah beshabbat. mihu, poh irenu bgd"d y", darkan shel kol bene-adam lekassot pi hechabiyyot baabanim shehem lebanim serupim; veetzlenu shekicha kissuy baabanim tepe min chatikot shel nesarim; velaken zo shekkissa bah pi hechabit bechol, muttar letaltelah, dachashib dabar sheddarko laasoto kissuy. vekol zeh bekissuy hakkelim, abal kissuy qarqaot kegon bor vedut vekayyotze, "p shettiqqenu veasa bo maaseh, vegam nishtammesh bo peamim rabbot bechol, asur letaltelo, ella im ken yesh lo bet achiza sheochazin bo kaasher mesirin oto min habbor, shezzeh mokicha alayv shehu asuy lehittaltel veyesh alayv shem keli. vekissuy hakkelim haqqeburim baqqarqa legamre, dinam kekissuy haqqarqaot, sheggazeru al ellu mippene ellu; abal keli sheeno qabur baqqarqa legamre, "p shehu mechubbar laqqarqa, kissuy shello eno tzarik bet achiza vekannizkar kol zeh besiman shch.

clarification.explanation: An object with no designation as a "vessel" at all, which was made into a lid for another vessel — acquires the status of a vessel and may be handled like other vessels, provided it was fashioned and prepared for this purpose through a clear act demonstrating it is designated for this role (even if not yet actually used for covering). And if it was already used for covering in practice before the Sabbath, even once — this alone suffices to give it the status of a vessel, even without any preparatory act. But this is true only for something normally made into a lid, such as a piece of wood (a board). By contrast, something not normally made into a lid — such as a stone used to cover the mouth of a barrel — even if it was used for this many times during the week, it is forbidden to handle it on the Sabbath. Nevertheless, Rabbi Yosef Chaim notes that in Baghdad the local custom is to cover barrel mouths specifically with stones (fired bricks) more than with wooden boards — and therefore for them such a stone is considered "something normally used this way," and it is permitted to handle it. Regarding covers for openings in the ground (such as a pit or pool) — even if they were fashioned and used many times, it is forbidden to handle them, unless they have a handle proving they are designated for handling. Vessels entirely buried in the ground — have the same law as ground covers (one decree due to the other); but a vessel not entirely buried in the ground — its cover does not require a handle.
takeaways: An object prepared or already used even once as a lid for a vessel acquires the status of a vessel and may be handled.
This applies only to something normally made into a lid; something not normally so (like a stone) is forbidden, unless it is the local custom.
Covers for pits and ground openings require a handle to permit handling them; a vessel entirely buried in the ground has the same law as the ground itself.

paragraphs: Muttar lachtok qishre hashshappud sheqqosherim battala o op hatztzeluyim bo. veken opot memullaim shetteparem, muttar lachtok chut hattepira. veken chut shemmaabirin bo teenim veqosheran shene rashin, demuttar lechateko. veken kelim kemo shidda veteba shekkissuy shellahem qashur bechebel, muttar lachtok hachebel apillu besakkin, o lehapqio kede lepatecham liqqach mah shebbetokam. vegam muttar lehattir haqqesher, shehare eno qesher shel qeyama, shehu asuy lehattiro tadir. veap shehachebel asuy lechabber hakkissuy im hakkeli, ukeshechoteko o mapqio hare zeh soter chibburam - en bazeh mishshum setira, lepi shehachebel hu chibbur garua sheeno chazaq kol kak, vahare zeh soter binyan garua, veen setira bekelim ella keshessoter binyan gamur. lepikak, potachat shel etz veshel matteket shehem chazaqim, asur lehapqia uleshabber im neebad hammapteach, dezehu setira gemura, vaasura apillu bekelim; umihu, muttar lepatecham bemachat o masmer vekayyotze. veken asur lehasir hatztzirim sheachore hatteba kede liptoach hatteba, mippene shehem tequim bechozeq vahare zeh setira gemura; veraq "y nakeri bimqom metzuvveh vetzorek oto hayyom, yesh lehaqel, ben bishbirat happotachat, ben bahasarat hatztzirim.

clarification.explanation: It is permitted to cut the strings tying a lamb or roasted fowl to the spit, and likewise the sewing thread in a stuffed fowl, and likewise a string used to string figs together for tying — it is permitted to cut it. Likewise with vessels such as a chest whose lid is tied with a rope — it is permitted to cut the rope even with a knife, or to tear it, in order to open it and take out what is inside; and it is also permitted to untie the knot itself, since it is not a "permanent knot" but one made to be untied regularly. The reason there is no prohibition of "demolishing" here even though the rope connects the lid to the vessel: the connection by rope is a weak and flimsy connection, and the prohibition of demolishing applies only to dismantling an actual, sturdy structure. By contrast, a lock made of wood or metal that is sturdy — if the key is lost, it is forbidden to break it or force it apart, since this is complete demolishing, forbidden even for vessels; but it is permitted to open it with a needle or nail and the like (without breaking it). Likewise it is forbidden to remove the hinges at the back of a chest in order to open it, since they are firmly wedged in and their removal is considered complete demolishing; only through a gentile, for the sake of a commandment or an urgent need of that same day, may one be lenient — both regarding breaking the lock and removing the hinges.
takeaways: Loose tying strings (on roasted meat, a stuffed fowl, figs, or a rope-tied chest lid) may be cut or untied.
A sturdy lock (wood/metal) may not be broken if the key is lost, but may be opened gently with a needle or nail.
Removing sturdy hinges from the back of a chest is forbidden as complete demolishing; permitted only through a gentile for a commandment or urgent same-day need.

paragraphs: Chotalot shel temarim o gerogarot, dehaynu kelim haasuyim mikkappot temarim, umannichim betokam temarim, veqorin otam bearbe "ketzap" (salseleah) - im hakkissuy qashur bachebel, muttar lehapqia hachebel o lechateko; vaapillu gupan shel kelim ellu muttar lehapqia velachtok, dehave keshober egozim usheqedim bishbil haokel shebbahem.

clarification.explanation: Baskets ("khutalot") made of palm fronds, in which dates or dried figs (called in Arabic "khasaf") are placed — if their lid is tied with a rope, it is permitted to cut or untie the rope. Moreover, it is even permitted to break and cut the body of the basket itself in order to reach the dates inside, since this is considered like cracking nuts or almonds to reach the food inside them — an act permitted for the sake of the food.
takeaways: A rope-tied lid on a basket of dates — may be cut or untied.
It is even permitted to break the basket's body itself to reach the food, following the law of cracking a nut's shell.

paragraphs: Keshem sheasur liptoach kol neqeb bikli beshabbat, kak asur listom kol neqeb, mippene shehu kimtaqqen keli. velaken asur listom neqeb hechabit shehayyayin o shear mashqeh yotzein mimmennu, apillu bedabar sheen bo issur merucha; vekol shekken deasur listom beshaava, deikka bazeh issur memareach; vaapillu hayeta hashshaava banneqeb mibbeod yom venapela beshabbat, asur lehachazirah.

clarification.explanation: Just as it is forbidden to open a new hole in a vessel on the Sabbath, so it is also forbidden to plug an existing hole, since this is considered repairing the vessel. Therefore it is forbidden to plug a hole in a barrel from which wine or another beverage is leaking, even with a material that carries no prohibition of smoothing; and all the more so it is forbidden to plug it with wax, since this carries the additional prohibition of "smearing" (spreading a soft substance). And even if the wax had been in the hole before the Sabbath and fell out on the Sabbath, it is forbidden to put it back in place.
takeaways: It is forbidden to plug a hole in a barrel on the Sabbath, even with a dry material that is not smeared.
Plugging with wax is more severe — it also carries the prohibition of smearing.
Even wax that was in the hole before the Sabbath and fell out may not be put back on the Sabbath.

paragraphs: Machat shennitaqqema, asur lehashvotah beyado. veken batte-enayim shenniptechu harbeh, asur lehadqam bayyad, dehave metaqqen mana; vetzarik lehazhir haam beelleh, shehem debarim hammetzuyim.

clarification.explanation: A bent needle — it is forbidden to straighten it by hand on the Sabbath. Likewise eyeglasses ("eye-houses") that have opened too wide — it is forbidden to tighten them by hand, since this is considered "repairing a vessel." Rabbi Yosef Chaim emphasizes that the public should be warned about these matters, since they are common occurrences in daily life.
takeaways: A bent needle — may not be straightened on the Sabbath, considered repairing a vessel.
Eyeglasses that opened too wide — may not be tightened by hand on the Sabbath.

paragraphs: Asur leishah liqloa saarot roshah, dedame lebinyan; vehu haddin deasur listor qeliat searah, dedame lesoter. venashim haholekim litbila belel-shabbat, lo yiqleu searot rosham, ella yeshalshelum ben hechaluq uben habbeged, veyilbeshu pea nakerit shehi qelua veomedet mibbeod yom. veotam haashirim sheddarkam litlot takshit zahab al-yede chutin sheqqoleim otam besaarotehen sheyyihyu seruchin laachorehem, lo yaasu ken beshabbat, ella yitperu chutin ellu shettaluy bahem hattakshit bekoba shellahem sheqqorin bearbe "piyyes" (tarbush, migbaat adumma lelo shulayim), veaz yihyeh gam ken sarucha al gabbam beshabbat kedarko.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for a woman to braid her hair on the Sabbath, since this resembles the labor of "building"; and for the same reason it is also forbidden to undo an existing braid, since this resembles "demolishing." Therefore women who go to immerse in the mikveh on Sabbath night should not braid their hair, but rather let it hang freely between the undergarment and the outer garment, and if they want their hair gathered, they should wear a wig braided in advance (before the Sabbath), since the wig is already braided and there is no prohibition of building in wearing it. Likewise, wealthy women who were accustomed to hang gold jewelry by threads braided into their hair so that the jewelry dangles behind their heads — should not do this on the Sabbath (since this is new braiding); rather, they should sew the threads from which the jewelry hangs onto the cap ("fez" — a red turban) in advance, so that the jewelry remains dangling down their back via the cap even on the Sabbath, without needing to braid.
takeaways: It is forbidden to braid hair on the Sabbath (resembling building) and also forbidden to undo an existing braid (resembling demolishing).
The solution for immersion on Sabbath night: let the hair hang free, or wear a wig braided in advance.
Gold jewelry hung by threads in the hair should be sewn in advance to the cap, not to the hair itself.

paragraphs: Makbesh, shehu shene luchot shekkobeshin bahem begadim: im hu shel baal habbayit, muttar lepatecho laqachat habbegadim letzorek bo bayyom, veshel ummanin asur liptoach, mishshum dezeh darko lihyot mehuddaq bechozeq, upetichato domeh listira; vaapillu patucha mibbeod yom, yesh oserin laqach mimmennu habbegadim, gezera shemma yiptach atta; mihu letzorek harbeh, yesh lehaqel bepatucha mibbeod yom.

clarification.explanation: A garment press made of two boards that press garments between them to smooth them: if the press belongs to the homeowner himself, it is permitted to open it to take garments from it for that day's need. But if the press belongs to a professional craftsman (a professional launderer), it is forbidden to open it, since such a press is normally very tightly fastened, and opening it resembles an act of demolishing. And even if the press was already open before the Sabbath, some forbid taking garments from it on the Sabbath, out of concern that one might come to close and reopen it now. But when there is great need, one may be lenient and take garments from a press that was already open before the Sabbath.
takeaways: A private garment press (belonging to the homeowner) — permitted to open on the Sabbath for that day's need.
A professional craftsman's press — forbidden to open, since opening it resembles demolishing something tightly fastened.
If the press was already open before the Sabbath and there is great need, one may be lenient in taking garments from it.
